body: Flag: MIXED. Ports-to-power conglomerate built with heavy debt and concentrated promoter holdings (60-75%). Hindenburg (24-Jan-2023) alleged stock manipulation via Mauritius-linked FPIs and undisclosed related parties; ~$150bn market cap fell, the Rs 20,000 cr FPO was withdrawn. Regulator record: the Supreme Court (Jan-2024) declined an SIT/CBI probe and left it to SEBI; SEBI (Sep-2025) dismissed the Hindenburg related-party/fund-routing allegations (Adicorp, Milestone, Rehvar loans) finding no violation; SEBI's minimum-public-shareholding case ended (Sep-2026) with Vinod Adani cleared and Gautam Adani plus four group companies settling for ~Rs 1.48 cr (settlement = no admission). Still open: SEBI's probe of whether 13 overseas FPIs were genuine public holders -- SEBI rejected all 13 settlement applications (Aug-2026). US: DOJ bribery indictment (Nov-2024) dismissed with prejudice (Aug-2026); SEC civil case moved to proposed final judgments with ~$18 m penalties (May-2026, verify final). Good conduct post-2023: promoters prepaid ~$2.15bn of share-backed loans (pledges in Adani Ports to ~0, Adani Power ~25% -> ~1%), GQG and other long-only investors came in, Adani exited Adani Wilmar (2025). Growth continues via acquisitions (Ambuja/ACC, Orient Cement, Jaiprakash Associates via IBC 2026). Risks: high capex and debt, related-party flows among group cos, valuation, political-proximity perception. Investor read: the worst allegations were not upheld by Indian or US authorities, but disclosure/ownership opacity remains the core issue.

data.regulator_findings: SEBI Sep-2025: no violation on Hindenburg RPT allegations; MPS case settled Sep-2026; FPI probe open
data.status_2026: FPI-ownership probe continuing after settlements rejected (Aug-2026)
